chunks: And he saw phlegm in the mosque, so he walked to it with a palm-stick from the palm-branches of Ibn Ṭāb and scraped it off, then he returned backward and continued his prayer.
And al-Sadiq عليه السلام said: 'And this opens many doors regarding the prayer.'

key_terms.أَبْوَاباً: doors, i.e. multiple legal applications or rulings
key_terms.الْقَهْقَرَى: backward, meaning he returned without turning away fully
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدِ: the mosque, the sacred place in which the incident occurred
key_terms.بِعُرْجُونٍ: with a palm-stick or stalk used to remove the impurity
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer), which he then continued
key_terms.نُخَامَةً: phlegm or spittle found in the mosque
key_terms.يَفْتَحُ: opens, meaning establishes broader legal implications

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith show about moving or doing small necessary actions during salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم removed filth from the mosque during salat (prayer) and then resumed his prayer. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام indicates that this incident establishes broader legal latitude for limited necessary actions within salat (prayer).
